stem: The `City` field has both Cologne and Köln as separate members, and the analyst wants them to count as one city in the view. Which action does this?

options.text: Right-click the `City` field and choose Create Hierarchy
options.rationale: A hierarchy stacks fields for drilling. It does not merge members of one field.

options.text: Select both marks and choose Create Set to build an In/Out field
options.rationale: A set only marks members as In or Out. Both spellings would still be separate members.

options.text: Select both city headers and click the group icon
options.rationale: The group icon combines the selected members into a single group, which is what merging spellings needs.

options.text: Drag `City` to the Filters shelf and keep only Köln
options.rationale: Filtering removes the Cologne rows rather than combining them with Köln.

explanation: A group combines related members of one field into a single member. You can start one from selected marks or headers, using the paperclip group icon on the tooltip or the toolbar.

stem: Which Data pane menu path starts a group on a dimension?

options.text: Right-click the field, then Create > Group
options.rationale: In the Data pane, Create > Group opens the dialog where you pick the members to combine.

options.text: Right-click the field, then Create > Set
options.rationale: Create > Set opens the set dialog, which defines an In/Out subset and combines nothing.

options.text: Right-click the field, then Create Hierarchy
options.rationale: Create Hierarchy starts a drill path of several fields; it doesn't combine members.

options.text: Right-click the field, then Show Filter
options.rationale: Show Filter adds a filter card to the sheet and does not create any new field.

explanation: Groups can be created from marks or headers in the view or from the Data pane. In the Data pane you right-click a dimension, choose Create > Group, then select the members to combine.

stem: An analyst selects the `Comedy` and `Drama` headers and clicks the group icon without naming anything. What name does the group get?

options.text: It stays unnamed until the analyst opens Edit Group and types a name
options.rationale: A default name is created automatically, so the group is never unnamed.

options.text: It is named `Group 1`, and the name cannot be changed afterwards
options.rationale: The default name comes from the member names, and the group can be renamed.

options.text: It takes the name of the field, such as `Genre (group)`, and the members are hidden
options.rationale: The default name uses the combined member names, and the members are not hidden by naming.

options.text: A default name built from the combined member names, which Rename can change
options.rationale: Tableau generates the name from the members. Rename lets you replace it with something clearer.

explanation: When you group, Tableau names the group by joining the member names. Use Rename in the dialog to give it a better name.

stem: The Driftlight content team created a genre group last month and now wants to move one genre out of it. Where do they do that?

options.text: Right-click the group in the Data pane, choose Create Set, and untick the member
options.rationale: Create Set builds a new In/Out field and leaves the group itself unchanged.

options.text: Choose Edit Group on the group field, select the member and click Ungroup
options.rationale: Edit Group is where you select members and click Ungroup to take them out of the group.

options.text: Drag the group field onto another field in the Data pane
options.rationale: Dropping a field onto another creates a hierarchy and does not change group membership.

options.text: Open the Filters shelf, edit the group's filter and exclude the member
options.rationale: A filter hides the member from the view. It does not take it out of the group definition.

explanation: Existing groups are edited through the group field's Edit Group command. There you select members and click Ungroup, or rename the group.

stem: The content team wants three named genre groups, with every remaining genre lumped into one bucket. Which setting does this?

options.text: Include 'Other' in the Edit Group dialog
options.rationale: Include 'Other' groups all remaining, non-grouped members into an Other group.

options.text: Show In/Out of Set on the Color shelf
options.rationale: Show In/Out of Set belongs to sets, and it gives two categories, not named groups.

options.text: Add the remaining genres to a context filter
options.rationale: A context filter removes rows from the view. The leftovers would disappear and not be bucketed.

options.text: Create a hierarchy with `Genre` at the top level
options.rationale: A hierarchy adds drill levels and does not collect leftover members.

explanation: Include 'Other' keeps a few named groups and puts the long tail of members into one extra group. It is useful when most members are not worth showing individually.

stem: Which statement describes a group in Tableau?

options.text: It splits a dimension into In and Out members based on a subset
options.rationale: That describes a set, which marks each member as In or Out.

options.text: It stacks related dimensions so the view can be drilled down and up
options.rationale: That describes a hierarchy, which uses the + and - icons to drill.

options.text: It combines members of a field into larger categories
options.rationale: A group merges members, such as several genres into one broader category.

options.text: It removes marks from the view by testing a condition on a measure
options.rationale: That describes a filter. A group changes how members are categorized and removes none.

explanation: Groups, sets and hierarchies are easy to mix up. A group merges members into new categories, a set marks In or Out, and a hierarchy orders dimensions for drilling.

stem: Which two actions start the creation of a group? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Drag a dimension onto another dimension in the Data pane
options.rationale: This starts a hierarchy, not a group.

options.text: Select marks in the view and click the group icon on the tooltip
options.rationale: The tooltip's paperclip icon groups the selected marks.

options.text: Right-click a mark and choose Create Set
options.rationale: This makes a set with In and Out members.

options.text: Right-click a dimension in the Data pane and choose Create > Group
options.rationale: This opens the group dialog from the Data pane.

options.text: Drag a dimension to the Filters shelf
options.rationale: This opens the Filter dialog and creates no group.

explanation: You can create a group from selected marks or headers in the view, or from a dimension in the Data pane. The other actions create a hierarchy, a set or a filter.

stem: Which two things can an analyst do in the Edit Group dialog? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Select members and click Ungroup
options.rationale: Ungroup takes the selected members out of the group.

options.text: Define the members by a Top N rule on a measure
options.rationale: Top rules belong to the dynamic set dialog, not to groups.

options.text: Switch the group to a fixed or dynamic type
options.rationale: Groups have no fixed or dynamic type. That distinction applies to sets.

options.text: Add the group to a context filter so it runs first
options.rationale: Context is set from a filter's menu and is not an option in the group dialog.

options.text: Include 'Other' to collect the non-grouped members
options.rationale: This option puts the remaining members into an Other group.

explanation: Edit Group lets you rename the group, ungroup members and include an Other group for the rest. Rules based on measures belong to sets and filters.

stem: Which two Driftlight requests call for a group? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Flag the top 20 titles by minutes watched against all the others
options.rationale: An In/Out flag defined by a Top rule is a set.

options.text: Drill from Type down to Genre in the same view
options.rationale: Drill paths are built with a hierarchy.

options.text: Combine the München and Munich spellings into one city
options.rationale: Merging several members into one category is a group.

options.text: Bundle genres into a Scripted and an Unscripted category
options.rationale: Broader categories made from members are groups.

options.text: Show only sessions that started on a TV
options.rationale: Restricting rows is a filter, not a group.

explanation: A group merges members into new categories. Flagging members In or Out is a set, drilling is a hierarchy, and removing rows is a filter.

stem: An analyst selects five title marks in a bar chart and wants to save exactly those titles as a subset. What should they do?

options.text: Click the group icon on the tooltip and rename the group
options.rationale: A group merges the five titles into one member, which hides them individually.

options.text: Drag `Title` onto `Genre` in the Data pane and name it
options.rationale: This builds a hierarchy of two fields, not a subset.

options.text: Choose Keep Only, then Add to Context on the filter
options.rationale: Keep Only filters the view and does not leave a reusable In/Out field.

options.text: Right-click the marks and choose Create Set
options.rationale: Creating a set from marks gives a fixed set made of the selected members.

explanation: Sets are made from marks with Create Set. The set holds the selected members, and each other member of the field is Out of the set.

stem: Marketing wants a set of the top 20 titles by minutes that updates each week as viewing changes. How is it built?

options.text: Select the top 20 title marks in a bar chart and choose Create Set
options.rationale: A set made from selected marks is fixed and never updates.

options.text: Use Create > Set on `Title` and define it on the Top tab
options.rationale: A set defined on the Top tab is dynamic, so it follows the data.

options.text: Select the top 20 titles and group them with the paperclip icon
options.rationale: A group merges the titles into one member and does not follow the data.

options.text: Drag `Title` onto `Minutes Watched` in the Data pane
options.rationale: Dropping a field onto another does not build a set.

explanation: Dynamic sets are created from a dimension in the Data pane and defined by the General, Condition or Top tab. Condition and Top rules are recomputed when the underlying data changes.

stem: A set was created by selecting marks. Later, new sessions are added to the data. What happens to the set?

options.text: Its members stay exactly as they were selected
options.rationale: A set made from marks is fixed, so its members do not change when the data does.

options.text: It recalculates its members from the new data
options.rationale: Only dynamic sets, defined by a condition or a top N, recalculate.

options.text: It becomes a group made of the selected members
options.rationale: Sets and groups are different fields, and a set never converts into a group.

options.text: It is deleted and has to be created again from the new marks
options.rationale: Fixed sets persist as fields in the Data pane.

explanation: A fixed set keeps the members chosen at creation. A dynamic set follows the data because it is defined by a rule instead of a list of marks.

stem: The analyst wants a set of every title where `SUM(Minutes Watched)` is above a threshold. Which tab of the set dialog defines this?

options.text: General
options.rationale: General is for picking individual members from a list, or Use all.

options.text: Top
options.rationale: Top limits members to a number or a percentage by a measure, not to a threshold.

options.text: Condition
options.rationale: The Condition tab defines a rule on a measure that decides which members are included.

options.text: Fixed
options.rationale: The set dialog has no Fixed tab. A fixed set is the kind made from marks.

explanation: The dynamic set dialog has General, Condition and Top tabs. A threshold such as `SUM(Minutes Watched) > 20000` is a Condition. A limit like the top 10 is a Top definition.

stem: A set named `Top Titles` is on the Color shelf, and the analyst wants only two colors: titles in the set and everything else. What should they choose?

options.text: Right-click the set and choose Create Hierarchy
options.rationale: Hierarchies are built from fields dropped on each other, not from a set.

options.text: Right-click the set and choose Include 'Other'
options.rationale: Include 'Other' belongs to the group dialog.

options.text: Right-click the set and choose Show Members in Set
options.rationale: This lists every member individually, so there would be many colors.

options.text: Right-click the set and choose Show In/Out of Set
options.rationale: This aggregates the members into In and Out categories.

explanation: A set in the view can show its members or collapse them into In and Out. Show In/Out of Set compares the subset against the rest.

stem: Which statement about creating sets is correct?

options.text: A set from the Data pane can use several dimensions, and one from marks only one
options.rationale: This is reversed. Marks can span dimensions and the Data pane route cannot.

options.text: A set from marks can use several dimensions, and one from the Data pane uses a single dimension
options.rationale: Marks may carry several dimensions, while the Data pane route works on one dimension.

options.text: Both ways create dynamic sets that update when the underlying data changes
options.rationale: Only the Data pane route, with a Condition or Top rule, gives a dynamic set.

options.text: Both ways create fixed sets whose members are chosen from a list of marks
options.rationale: The Data pane route offers dynamic definitions as well, through the General, Condition and Top tabs.

explanation: Marks give you fixed sets that can cover several dimensions. The Data pane route works on one dimension at a time and can be dynamic.

stem: The analyst selects some marks and wants the set to hold every member except those marks. What helps?

options.text: Choose Exclude these members instead
options.rationale: This option defines the set as everything except the selected members.

options.text: Choose Show In/Out of Set after dragging the set to the Rows shelf
options.rationale: This only changes how a set is displayed after it exists.

options.text: Use Keep Only on the selected marks, which filters the view
options.rationale: Keep Only filters the view and creates no set.

options.text: Create a group from the selected marks and tick Include 'Other'
options.rationale: A group merges members, so it cannot produce an exclusion set.

explanation: The Create Set dialog lets you invert the selection with Exclude these members instead. The result is still a fixed set.

stem: Which two statements describe a dynamic set? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: It is defined on the General, Condition or Top tab
options.rationale: These tabs are the three ways to define it.

options.text: It is created by right-clicking marks and choosing Create Set
options.rationale: That route creates a fixed set.

options.text: It always spans several dimensions
options.rationale: A dynamic set from the Data pane is based on a single dimension.

options.text: Its members change when the underlying data changes
options.rationale: This is what makes it dynamic.

options.text: Its members never change once it exists
options.rationale: That is the behavior of a fixed set.

explanation: Dynamic sets are defined by rules instead of a hand-picked list, so they follow the data. They come from the Data pane and are based on one dimension.

stem: Which two Driftlight requests call for a set? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Merge Cologne and Köln into one city
options.rationale: Merging members is a group.

options.text: Compare the top 20 titles by minutes with every other title
options.rationale: An In/Out split by a Top rule is a dynamic set.

options.text: Drill from Type down to Genre
options.rationale: Drilling uses a hierarchy.

options.text: Let viewers pick a Device from a card
options.rationale: A filter card is Show Filter, not a set.

options.text: Flag titles where `SUM(Minutes Watched)` exceeds a threshold
options.rationale: A rule on a measure is a Condition on a set.

explanation: A set divides a dimension into In and Out, which makes comparisons of a subset against the rest simple. Merging, drilling and filter cards use other tools.

stem: Where does the analyst start in the Data pane to create a hierarchy from `Type` and `Genre`?

options.text: Right-click `Type` and choose Create > Group, then add `Genre`
options.rationale: Create > Group merges members of one field and does not link two fields.

options.text: Right-click `Type` and choose Create > Set, then add `Genre`
options.rationale: A set marks members of one dimension as In or Out and cannot nest fields.

options.text: Drop `Genre` directly on `Type`, then name the hierarchy
options.rationale: Dropping a field on another creates the hierarchy and prompts for a name.

options.text: Drag both fields to the Filters shelf at the same time
options.rationale: The Filters shelf removes data and builds no drill path.

explanation: A hierarchy is created in the Data pane by dropping one field on top of another. Add the further fields in order from general to detailed.

stem: A dimension sits inside a folder in the Data pane. How can the analyst start a hierarchy from it?

options.text: Right-click the field and select Create > Group
options.rationale: This merges members rather than ordering fields.

options.text: Right-click the field and select Show Filter
options.rationale: This adds a filter card and creates no field.

options.text: Drag the folder onto the Rows shelf and click + on it
options.rationale: Folders are not hierarchies, and + only drills one that already exists.

options.text: Right-click the field and select Create Hierarchy
options.rationale: For a field inside a folder, Create Hierarchy is on its right-click menu.

explanation: Dragging one field onto another is one way to build a hierarchy. For a field inside a folder, the right-click Create Hierarchy command is the alternative.

stem: Which two steps are part of creating a hierarchy in the Data pane? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Select two marks and click the paperclip group icon
options.rationale: This creates a group of members.

options.text: Right-click a mark and choose Create Set
options.rationale: This creates a set from the mark.

options.text: Drop one field directly on top of another and name the hierarchy
options.rationale: This starts the hierarchy and gives it a name.

options.text: Drag further fields in, ordered from general to detailed
options.rationale: The order sets the drill path, such as Type before Genre.

options.text: Drag the dimension to the Filters shelf
options.rationale: This opens a filter dialog and builds no hierarchy.

explanation: Creating a hierarchy means stacking dimensions in the Data pane, from the most general at the top to the most detailed. In the view, + and - on the hierarchy field then drill down and up.
